**Triage: lands in `.github/prompts/component.prompt.md`; `domain:devx`; `priority:p2` — it teaches retired keys to every AI that reads it.**

`:71` still lists `view:kanban` and `view:gantt` among the component keys. Both are **retired** — objectui#8802 retired the bare `kanban` node type and objectui#8008 the bare `gantt` registration (maintainer rulings 2026-09-09, delivered by PR #8865); because `ComponentRegistry.register` stores both the namespaced key and a bare-`type` fallback, `view:kanban` / `view:gantt` retired with them.

⇒ p2, and the reason is the audience: this is an **instruction file read by agents**, so a stale key here is not one wrong page — it is every future generated component reaching for a key the registry no longer answers. That is the metadata-trap class operating at its highest leverage.

⇒ Correct the list. ⚠️ **Re-derive it from the registry** rather than deleting the two named keys — the card measured the two it noticed, and a hand list that has drifted once will drift again.

### ⚠️ Recorded, ⛔ not filed as a second card here

`.github/prompts/**` is an **agent-instruction surface that is NOT in the governed register**. Verified on objectstack `origin/main`, `GOVERNED_SURFACES` enumerates `docs/adr/`, `.claude/`, `skills/`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` — and nothing under `.github/prompts/`. ⇒ a file that steers every AI contributor can be changed without the governed-merge path that `AGENTS.md` gets. That is a register gap, ⛔ not this card's to fix; it belongs to the skills lane and is named in this round's report rather than carded unilaterally.

`Size/model suggestion:` S.

|:--|--:|
| `view:*` keys in the generated `known-schema-types.ts` | **23**, and ⛔ **`view:kanban` and `view:gantt` are both among them** |

⇒ the registry **answers** `view:kanban`. A derivation that asks 「what does the registry answer」 reproduces the trap exactly, because the trap **is** that the registry answers with a placeholder panel instead of a board. ⭐ The card says this itself: 「an AI reading this prompt writes a document that passes the repository's own validator and **draws nothing**」.

## ⭐ So the real judgement, named here rather than discovered at review

This prompt teaches **what to author**. The generated list is 「what resolves」, and those two sets differ by exactly the placeholders. ⇒ the derivation has to distinguish **a key a real renderer answers** from **a key a placeholder answers**, and the prompt must teach only the first.

⛔ Deleting the two keys the card noticed is the option triage rejected. ⛔ Re-deriving from the generated list is a no-op. ⭐ The shape that satisfies both is a derivation over a population that **excludes the placeholder registrations** — and whatever you build, it has to be able to **fail**.

## Premises

1. The offending line is the **Keys** bullet under 「View Layouts (`view:*`)」; there is a **second** `view:*` Keys bullet further down (form layouts) which the card does ⛔ **not** mention — ⚠️ check it before you decide your scope is one line.
2. ⭐ `.github/prompts/**` is **NOT governed** — verified against the guard's own `GOVERNED_SURFACES`, which has exactly five entries and none of them is `.github/`. ⇒ ordinary queue, ⛔ not draft-only. ⚠️ Triage recorded the register **gap** deliberately and ⛔ did not card it; it belongs to the skills lane. ⛔ Not yours.
3. No gate reads this file today. ⇒ whatever keeps it true has to be **added**, or its absence stated plainly.
